the morphological plasticity of the HNS is the consequence of an interplay of several factors, including the presence of PSA-NCAM and tenascin-C, which may serve to modulate extracellular ionic and volume transmission.
PSA-NCAM and tenascin-C are likely to be involved in neuronal-glial and synaptic remodeling, but their role remains to be elucidated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

morphological plasticity of the adult HNS is a dynamic process that modifies neuronal-glial and synaptic relationships, thereby altering extracellular ionic and chemical environments, and synaptic transmission.

activity-dependent morphological changes in the adult HNS are mediated by dynamic interactions among neurons, astrocytes and synapses that are regulated, in part, by cell surface and extracellualar matrix adhesion molecules.
morphological plasticity in the HNS is an example of a highly dynamic and functional system that can be modified by the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adult brain, like the developing brain, is a dynamic system in which the cellular and extracellular milieu are constantly changing.
the adult HNS is not a static structure but rather a dynamic system in which the neuronal and glial compartments undergo activity-dependent remodeling that has direct functional consequences.
the adult brain, including the hypothalamus, continues to undergo activity-dependent morphological changes that are likely to have important functional implications.
